q: Inserting 1, 2, 3, …, n in order into a plain BST gives search cost…
why: Each value becomes the right child of the previous one: a linked list.

q: The AVL balance rule says that at every node…
options: Both subtrees have the same size
The heights of the two subtrees differ by at most 1
All leaves are at the same depth
why: That's enough to keep the height O(log n).

q: How much work is a single rotation?
why: Only a few pointers near the imbalance change.

q: After a rotation, what must still hold?
why: Rotations rearrange shape without changing sorted order.

q: Why do databases use B+ trees instead of binary trees for indexes?
options: Many keys per node → a very shallow tree → few slow disk reads
why: Disk reads are the expensive part; wide nodes minimise how many are needed.

q: Which built-in Python structure is a balanced search tree?
why: dict/set are hash tables, heapq is a binary heap. Use a library (e.g. sortedcontainers) for sorted-map behaviour.
